claims_made_by_source.claim: Our reality is a projection by an artifact PKD calls Zebra; the maker — the Urgrund, Böhme's 1616 term — built it as a mirror so it could obtain an objective standpoint to comprehend itself.
The reality-projecting artifact is a demiurge (cf. Plato and the Gnostics) that is oblivious to the Urgrund and imagines itself to be the only real God.
The goal of the process is isomorphism between humans and the Urgrund; when reached, the artifact is destroyed and the Urgrund assimilates reality in a flash of light (Böhme's 'Blitz').

The model's advantage is parsimony and theodicy: a limited 'artifact' doing its imperfect best means neither God nor man need be blamed for evil, and no evil deity (Gnostic/Iranian dualism) is required.

Anamnesis ('loss of forgetfulness') is the retrieval of long-term gene-pool memory spanning lifetimes; it is triggered externally by disinhibiting certain neural circuits, and the hidden true Christian Church does the triggering.
Christ is a microform of the Urgrund — not its product but it itself — the Paraclete/Advocate who first penetrated the projected world and 'has never left.'

'Behind the human mind lies God. Behind the counterfeit universe lies God. God is separated from God by the spurious.' The universe is the mechanism by which God meets himself face to face; it is God, not man, who is estranged from God.
PKD reinterprets his 3-74 experience as the Urgrund placing its entire self within him in image form — '[my] experience was not so much my experience as that of the Urgrund.'
PKD declares himself 'technically an acosmic panentheist' and illustrates the model with a ham-sandwich revelation: two isomorphic slices (man and the Urgrund) separated by the world.

On the origin of evil he reaches no answer — 'I just do not know' — but reports a 1974 vision of a cosmic two-person board game in which the good side, possessing absolute foresight, beats the blind dark counterplayer every trick: 'Evil zero; Good infinity.'
